properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 3:52PM MDT until October 24 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Bernalillo County in central New Mexico...
Northwestern Torrance County in central New Mexico...
Southeastern Sandoval County in north central New Mexico...
Southwestern Santa Fe County in north central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 352 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Edgewood, Tijeras, Escabosa, Chilili, Sedillo, Tajique, Cedar
Crest, Sandia Park, Cedar Grove and Manzano.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:49PM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of the riverwalk in Farmington are
flooded. Local overbank flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 10.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM MDT Saturday was 11.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
evening and continue falling to 6.6 feet early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.0
feet on 05/14/1941.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 600 AM MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL SUNDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Mineral, CO; Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:49PM MDT until October 24 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County and Rio Grande County...

* WHEN...Until 615 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will continue along and near the Rio Grande this
afternoon, especially from near Del Norte to below Monte Vista.
Several roads remain closed and housing areas evacuated due to high
water. While many rivers and streams have crested this morning,
flooding and high flows will continue this afternoon and evening,
especially around Monte Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 340 PM MDT, Water levels along the Rio Grande remain high,
especially in the stretch from Del Norte to below Monte Vista,
although the river has crested and levels are forecast to remain
steady or slowly fall into evening.
- Highway 285 between Monte Vista and Center remains closed, as
well as Highway 112 between Del Norte and Center and Highway 160
between Wolf Creek Pass and South Fork. Please continue to heed
any road closures.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Rio Grande from Del Norte to Monte Vista.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 2:46PM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues. This
rainfall occurred on Wednesday and Thursday.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Sunday Night /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.
Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 240 PM MST /340 PM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall this evening. However, downstream
impacts will continue at Navajo Route 71 to Birdsprings through
at least Sunday.
- Flooding is occurring along the Little Colorado River.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 2:00pm MST /3:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.34 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: The river is cresting now and is forecast to fall
through this evening.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 3:38PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 337 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 18
miles east of Aneth, or 24 miles north of Shiprock, moving north at
50 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation and
outdoor objects is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Arriola, Towaoc, Yellow Jacket, and Lewis.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 491 in Colorado between mile markers 1 and 6, and
between mile markers 30 and 43.
U.S. Highway 160 in Colorado between mile markers 5 and 30.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:24PM MDT until October 24 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Sandoval County in north central New Mexico...
Northeastern McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 730 PM MDT.

* At 324 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 2 inches of rain have
fallen today on top of saturated soils from earlier rainfall over
previous days. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area through 6 PM MDT. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Torreon Navajo Mission, Ojo Encino and Torreon.

This includes Highway 550 between Mile Markers 73 and 89.
properties.instruction:
In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles. Find an alternate route.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Colleton; Charleston
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 5:03PM EDT until October 24 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one foot of
inundation above ground level along shorelines and tidal
waterways (7.4 to 7.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water at Charleston).
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level possible along shorelines and
tidal waterways (7.9 to 8.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM EDT Sunday through Sunday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Significant saltwater inundation will render
numerous roads impassable. Properties may also flood.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:13 PM today
and around 7:34 AM Sunday at Charleston. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Colleton; Charleston
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 5:03PM EDT until October 25 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one foot of
inundation above ground level along shorelines and tidal
waterways (7.4 to 7.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water at Charleston).
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level possible along shorelines and
tidal waterways (7.9 to 8.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM EDT Sunday through Sunday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Significant saltwater inundation will render
numerous roads impassable. Properties may also flood.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:13 PM today
and around 7:34 AM Sunday at Charleston. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Conejos, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 2:53PM MDT until October 24 at 5:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and its tributaries
continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 247 PM MDT, High water levels in area creeks and streams
continue, although many locations in the San Juan Mountains have
crested and have begun to slowly fall. Over the western portion
of the San Luis Valley, many streams and creeks are near crest
now and will slowly fall for the remainder of the day. The
Conejos River at Mogote has crested, but will likely remain above
flood stage until early Monday morning.
- Please heed all road closures and evacuation or shelter in place
orders.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Platoro, Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 4:48PM AST until October 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast beaches of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE SUNDAY NIGHT

Colorado...

remain above bankfull through midnight tonight. Additional rainfall
could cause the river to rise, but it is expected to continue
decreasing through Sunday.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 10.3 feet, Water is flowing over the yards of homes in
the San Juan River Village northeast of Pagosa Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 9.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is currently below minor flood stage but is
expected to remain above bankfull through midnight tonight. It is
expected to continue falling to 9.0 feet Sunday morning and 7.3
feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 600 AM MDT.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 1:34PM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Francisco Bay, Monterey
Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:07 AM
Sunday 10/25, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
